raw_response:
I am getting older now, so I do not want to toss money around. My land is only 4.1 mu, and with just two people in the house, I mainly do what has worked on my fields before and what the other farmers nearby are doing. Wheat and maize together are still the safest for me. Wheat gives a steady harvest, and after wheat I put in maize right away so the land does not sit empty. I have a well, so if the spring is dry I can still water, but pumping costs money, so I will not irrigate too many times unless the crop really needs it. For fertilizer, I will use a moderate amount, not the highest, because I need to watch cash. I would rather put enough to avoid the crop looking weak, but I will not chase very high yields.

For wheat, I will sow in early October like usual, using a common improved seed that people in the village use. I will put most fertilizer before sowing, then add some urea once in spring if the wheat color is not strong enough. I will water a few times at the important stages, especially before winter if the soil is dry, then around jointing or heading if there is not enough rain. After wheat harvest in June, I will plant maize quickly, because the turnaround is always tight. I will not do heavy tillage, just simple field preparation so I can get the maize in on time. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, give base fertilizer and one topdress, and irrigate only if summer rain is not enough. This way I keep things steady and do not spend more than my small farm can carry.
